title: PUBG Mobile Royale Pass Missions: Weekly Completion Plan
summary: Track Royale Pass milestones without buying unnecessary skips or missing claim steps.
intro: Royale Pass progression is easier to manage when you plan around the missions actually available on your account. Reward levels, seasons and mission timing change, so build a simple weekly checklist rather than copying an outdated route.

sections.heading: Read the current pass before setting a goal
paragraphs: Open the live Royale Pass screen and identify the season end date, mission categories, level requirements and reward tracks. Different tiers can have different purchase requirements or claim rules. Do not assume a reward shown near the end of the track can be obtained with the time you have left. Distinguish missions that are immediately accessible from ones that unlock later. A high-level reward preview is a goal, not evidence that progression will be automatic. Write down the few rewards you genuinely want instead of trying to complete every task for its own sake.
points: Check whether a mission must be claimed after completion.
Do not rely on season dates from a previous Royale Pass.

sections.heading: Group compatible missions into ordinary matches
paragraphs: Some missions can be progressed together while playing normally, while others may require a particular mode, map or action. Read their exact conditions before creating a route. If two objectives conflict, choose the one that suits your preferred gameplay and current available time. Avoid playing recklessly just to satisfy a mission when it damages your ranked goals or team coordination. When you play with friends, share the relevant objectives so the group can select a compatible mode without making one person wait through unrelated tasks.
points: Prioritize missions that overlap with your normal game sessions.
Verify progress in the pass screen after a qualifying match.

sections.heading: Estimate the remaining work realistically
paragraphs: Compare the levels or points you still need with the number of missions left and your available play sessions. Do not turn an uncertain reward into a guaranteed completion date. Some tasks may be difficult or depend on gameplay conditions, so leave a margin rather than assuming every attempt succeeds. If you are behind, decide whether the reward is still worth pursuing. A limited-time pass is entertainment, not an obligation to spend money or sacrifice sleep. Your own schedule matters more than a creator's completion speed.
points: Set a weekly time budget that you can maintain comfortably.
Keep a small buffer for missions that take longer than expected.

sections.heading: Avoid rushed premium upgrades
paragraphs: Before purchasing a pass or upgrade, inspect the exact rewards and the rules applying to your account. A paid track may offer extra cosmetics, but it does not erase every mission requirement unless the event explicitly states that. Compare the cost with the rewards you would actually use. Do not purchase skip levels solely because a countdown is visible; calculate what is still achievable through regular progression first. If a reward appears random or draw-based, separate that uncertainty from deterministic mission rewards.
points: Read the current price and qualifying conditions inside the game.
Do not spend to recover time already invested if the value is unclear.

sections.heading: Close the season with a claim checklist
paragraphs: Before the season ends, revisit completed missions and rewards that require a separate claim. Check whether unused tokens or special materials have their own expiry rules. Take a screenshot of the relevant progress screen for your records if something appears incorrect. If a task does not credit, confirm its mode, timing and eligibility before contacting official support. Once the season closes, focus on what you received rather than assuming every visual preview should be in your inventory. This process reduces avoidable frustration without encouraging unnecessary spending.
points: Review claim buttons and expiring materials before the deadline.
Treat the next season as a fresh plan rather than carrying over assumptions.
